title: A Noetherian filtered colimit of etale algebras has finite separable fibres
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $B=\varinjlim_{i\in J}B_i$ be a filtered colimit, in the category of commutative $A$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], of etale $A$-algebras $B_i$, i.e. of $A$-algebras such that $\operatorname{Spec}B_i\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-weil-affine-spectrum] (equivalently, by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine], $A\to B_i$ is an etale ring map in the sense of Stacks, Algebra, Definition 00U1). Assume $B$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ be a prime with residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Then there are only finitely many primes $\mathfrak q_1,\ldots,\mathfrak q_r\subset B$ ($r\ge0$) lying over $\mathfrak p$; the canonical ring map $B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\prod_{j=1}^r\kappa(\mathfrak q_j)$, $b\otimes\lambda\mapsto(\bar b\,\bar\lambda)_j$ ($\bar b$ the image of $b$ in $\kappa(\mathfrak q_j)$, $\bar\lambda$ the image of $\lambda$ under the map $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak q_j)$ induced by $A\to B$), is an isomorphism; and each field extension $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\subset\kappa(\mathfrak q_j)$ is separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension].

proof.text: Notation. Put $\kappa=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $C=B\otimes_A\kappa$, $C_i=B_i\otimes_A\kappa$, and for $i\in J$ and $u:i\to i'$ let $\gamma_i=\iota_i\otimes\mathrm{id}:C_i\to C$ and $\gamma_u=B(u)\otimes\mathrm{id}:C_i\to C_{i'}$, where $\iota_i:B_i\to B$ are the coprojections; these are homomorphisms of $\kappa$-algebras. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-tensor-elementwise] (with $R=A$, $N=\kappa$): (a) every element of $C$ is $\gamma_i(y)$ for some $i$ and $y\in C_i$; (b) if $y\in C_i$ and $\gamma_i(y)=0$, then $\gamma_u(y)=0$ for some $u:i\to i'$. So $C$ is the filtered colimit of the $C_i$.

proof.text: Each $C_i$ is a finite product of finite separable extensions of $\kappa$. Indeed, $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa\otimes_AB_i)\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change] (base change of $A\to B_i$ along $A\to\kappa$), and $\kappa\otimes_AB_i\cong B_i\otimes_A\kappa=C_i$ as $\kappa$-algebras by the symmetry of the tensor product. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product] there is a $\kappa$-algebra isomorphism $C_i\cong L_{i,1}\times\cdots\times L_{i,n_i}$ with each $L_{i,k}$ a finite separable algebraic field extension of $\kappa$.

proof.text: $C$ is reduced. Let $x\in C$ with $x^n=0$. By Step 1(a), $x=\gamma_i(y)$ with $y\in C_i$; then $\gamma_i(y^n)=x^n=0$, so by Step 1(b) $\gamma_u(y)^n=\gamma_u(y^n)=0$ for some $u:i\to i'$. As $C_{i'}$ is reduced (Step 3), $\gamma_u(y)=0$, and $x=\gamma_{i'}(\gamma_u(y))=0$.

proof.text: There are no strict inclusions between the primes of $C$; hence every prime of $C$ is both minimal and maximal. Let $\mathfrak Q\subseteq\mathfrak Q'$ be primes of $C$. For each $i$, $\gamma_i^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)\subseteq\gamma_i^{-1}(\mathfrak Q')$ are primes of $C_i$, so they are equal by Step 3. If $x\in\mathfrak Q'$, write $x=\gamma_i(y)$ (Step 1(a)); then $y\in\gamma_i^{-1}(\mathfrak Q')=\gamma_i^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)$, so $x\in\mathfrak Q$. Thus $\mathfrak Q=\mathfrak Q'$. Every prime is therefore minimal, and it is maximal, since it is contained in some maximal ideal, which is prime.

proof.text: $C$ has only finitely many primes $\mathfrak Q_1,\ldots,\mathfrak Q_r$ ($r\ge0$), all maximal. Indeed $C$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-noetherian], since $B$ is; so $C$ has finitely many minimal primes by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes], and by Step 5 every prime of $C$ is minimal and maximal.

proof.text: $C\cong\prod_{j=1}^rC_{\mathfrak Q_j}$ and each $C_{\mathfrak Q_j}$ is a field, equal to the residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak Q_j)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq] (with $I=0$) the nilradical of $C$ is the intersection of all primes, i.e. $\mathfrak Q_1\cap\cdots\cap\mathfrak Q_r$ (Step 6), and it is $0$ by Step 4. So the maximal ideals $\mathfrak Q_1,\dots,\mathfrak Q_r$ of $C$ satisfy the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-product-of-localizations-at-maximal], and the canonical map $C\to\prod_jC_{\mathfrak Q_j}$, $c\mapsto(c/1)_j$, into the localizations [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is an isomorphism of $\kappa$-algebras, each $C_{\mathfrak Q_j}$ a local ring. Each projection $\pi_j:C\to C_{\mathfrak Q_j}$ is surjective; $C_{\mathfrak Q_j}$ is reduced, being a factor of the reduced ring $C$; and every prime $\mathfrak P$ of $C_{\mathfrak Q_j}$ is maximal, because $C_{\mathfrak Q_j}/\mathfrak P\cong C/\pi_j^{-1}(\mathfrak P)$ is a field ($\pi_j^{-1}(\mathfrak P)$ is a prime, hence maximal, ideal of $C$). So the only prime of the local ring $C_{\mathfrak Q_j}$ is its maximal ideal $\mathfrak Q_jC_{\mathfrak Q_j}$, which by [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq] is its nilradical, i.e. $0$. Hence $C_{\mathfrak Q_j}=C_{\mathfrak Q_j}/\mathfrak Q_jC_{\mathfrak Q_j}=\kappa(\mathfrak Q_j)$ [def-weil-residue-field] is a field.

proof.text: Primes of $B$ over $\mathfrak p$ and the canonical isomorphism. Let $j_B:B\to C$, $b\mapsto b\otimes1$, and $\mathfrak q_j=j_B^{-1}(\mathfrak Q_j)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-residue-fields](1), $\mathfrak q_1,\dots,\mathfrak q_r$ are pairwise distinct and are all the primes of $B$ lying over $\mathfrak p$ (so there are finitely many), and $\mathfrak Q_j=\ker\psi_{\mathfrak q_j}$ with $\psi_{\mathfrak q_j}:C\to\kappa(\mathfrak q_j)$, $b\otimes\lambda\mapsto\bar b\,\bar\lambda$. By part (2) of that node, $\psi_{\mathfrak q_j}$ is the composite of $C\to\kappa(\mathfrak Q_j)$ with an isomorphism $\kappa(\mathfrak Q_j)\cong\kappa(\mathfrak q_j)$. Composing the isomorphism $C\cong\prod_j\kappa(\mathfrak Q_j)$ of Step 7 (whose $j$-th component is $C\to C_{\mathfrak Q_j}=\kappa(\mathfrak Q_j)$) with these isomorphisms shows that the canonical map $C\to\prod_j\kappa(\mathfrak q_j)$, $b\otimes\lambda\mapsto(\psi_{\mathfrak q_j}(b\otimes\lambda))_j=(\bar b\,\bar\lambda)_j$, is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Each $\kappa(\mathfrak q_j)/\kappa$ is separable algebraic. By Step 8, $\psi_j=\psi_{\mathfrak q_j}:C\to\kappa(\mathfrak q_j)$ is surjective and $\kappa$-linear for the $\kappa$-structure on $\kappa(\mathfrak q_j)$ given by $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak q_j)$. Let $\alpha\in\kappa(\mathfrak q_j)$; write $\alpha=\psi_j(x)$ and $x=\gamma_i(y)$ with $y\in C_i$ (Step 1(a)). The $\kappa$-algebra map $\psi_j\circ\gamma_i:C_i\to\kappa(\mathfrak q_j)$ has prime kernel $\mathfrak P$ (its target is a field), and by Step 3 $C_i/\mathfrak P\cong L_{i,k}$ for some $k$; so $\psi_j\circ\gamma_i$ induces a $\kappa$-embedding of fields $L_{i,k}\hookrightarrow\kappa(\mathfrak q_j)$ whose image contains $\alpha$. The preimage $\beta\in L_{i,k}$ of $\alpha$ is algebraic and separable over $\kappa$ (Step 2), and since a $\kappa$-embedding preserves polynomial relations, $\alpha$ has the same minimal polynomial over $\kappa$ as $\beta$, which is separable. Hence every element of $\kappa(\mathfrak q_j)$ is algebraic and separable over $\kappa$, i.e. $\kappa(\mathfrak q_j)/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension].

split_report.summary: Read Stacks More on Algebra Lemma 0AH1 (more-algebra.tex line 11236) and its proof, and the cited Algebra 00U3, 02LX/00KJ (through 00JA), 00E6, 0H9M, 00FN, 00FR, 00DD, 00D6, all checked in tags/tags. The statement agreed with Stacks (hypothesis: B Noetherian; conclusion: separable algebraic, not finite, residue extensions) and was only made precise: colimit taken in commutative A-algebras, 'etale A-algebra' spelled out as Spec B_i -> Spec A etale with the 00U1 equivalence cited, the 'canonical decomposition' written as the explicit map b(x)lambda -> (bbar lambdabar)_j, r >= 0 allowed, and the separable-algebraic definition cited. Proof written in nine steps following the Stacks proof: fibre as filtered colimit, fibres of the B_i finite products of finite separable extensions, facts on finite products of fields, reducedness, no specializations, Noetherian hence finitely many primes, product of fields via 00JA and the nilradical, identification with residue fields of the primes of B over p, separability. Five new nodes: 00U3 (Mathlib leaf Algebra.Etale.iff_exists_algEquiv_prod), 00FR (Mathlib leaf minimalPrimes.finite_of_isNoetherianRing), and unsplit nodes for the base change of a filtered colimit of algebras (00DD/00D6), the primes and residue fields of the fibre ring (00E6/0H9M; Mathlib has the prime part only) and Noetherianity of the fibre ring (00E6/00FN).

The fibre is a filtered colimit of finite products of finite separable extensions, hence reduced with incomparable primes, Noetherian with finitely many primes, so a product of its residue fields (00JA node), identified with the residue fields of the primes of B over p; separability passes to the colimit.
